overview: White plays 3.f4 against the ...Nc6 set-up, offering the e5 pawn to open the f-file and the b2 bishop. After 3...exf4 4.Nf3 Black can keep the pawn with ...g5, so White plays on development and the long diagonal. It is a speculative extension of the Larsen with little theory behind it.

white_ideas.idea: Win back f4 with Nf3 and Bxf4 or Nh4 while the b2 bishop looks down the long diagonal
Use the half-open f-file and quick development against the Black king

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...exf4 and ...g5
Challenge the centre with ...d5 and finish development before White gets going

typical_structures.structure: White pawn on f4 gone, Black pawn on f4/g5 chain with open e-file
Open centre with Bb2 aimed at g7

character.notes: After 3...exf4 the e-file opens and White is a pawn down chasing activity; both kings are exposed.

gambit.notes: White offers the e5 pawn with 3.f4; Black can keep it by ...g5.

soundness.notes: Black can simply take and hold the pawn, so White relies on surprise; engines favour Black.

structure.notes: The e- and f-pawns come off, leaving an open centre.

level.notes: Needs understanding of compensation rather than a long theory file.

plan_phrases: attack on the Black king via the f-file

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined with 3...Nf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. b3 e5 2. Bb2 Nc6 3. f4 Nf6
sublines_that_differ.how: No material changes hands and Black stands well.

character.reason: The f-file and an exposed king make a pawn-down attack with real risk for both.

gambit.reason: White gives the e5 pawn on purpose and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Engines prefer Black and the line scores mostly through surprise.

structure.reason: The e- and f-pawns trade off, so the game turns on open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly choose 3.f4 in this line.

level.reason: Dubious lines are not beginner choices and the theory is thin.

plans.reason: White pays a pawn for time and pressure on the kingside.
